svg.text: Three-node Raft HA: create/drop user replicates login authorization to every peer

g.text: create user alice, on the leader
create user alice, on the leader
await alice login on all three
await alice login on all three
drop user alice, on the leader
drop user alice, on the leader
a probe for a not-yet-replicated user
3 ArcadeDB containers on one Docker network, all given the same Raft server list.
All containers start in parallel; Testcontainers waits for each node's HTTP health probe.
Every node's cluster endpoint is polled once a second until one of them claims leadership.
GET /api/v1/cluster -> body contains "isLeader":true (the run fails after 60s)
An elected leader is not enough: a node still outside the Raft group would learn about the new user far too late.
Creating the user in that window commits on the majority while the late peer is absent
create user is a leader-only write, so it is addressed to the leader rather than forwarded over HTTP.
Replication is proved by an actual login on each node, probed no faster than the lockout policy allows.
pollInterval 10s > lockoutWindow/maxFailures (30s / 5): a faster loop would lock alice out and test the lockout instead
The user is dropped on the leader; the removal has to travel the same replication path.
The test passes only once alice is refused everywhere: a stale peer still granting access is the bug.
